一見すると古いFlashゲームのように見えるかもしれない。しかし、その古臭いUIの向こう側には、往年のRPGファンが探し求めていた「理想の沼」が広がっています。
反射神経はいりません。マッピングの苦行もありません。あるのは、純粋な戦略と育成、そして終わらない戦利品への渇望だけです。

 * Wizardryの深み × ハクスラの中毒性
本作の真髄は、「キャラクタービルド」と「装備収集」にあります。豊富なクラス、スキル、そして装備品。これらを組み合わせる楽しさは、まさに『Wizardry』などの古典的名作に通じる奥深さがあります。「あと1回だけ戦闘してからやめよう」と思っているうちに数時間が溶けている、そんな恐ろしい時間泥棒（褒め言葉）です。

 * 脳内設定が捗る！ 驚異のカスタマイズ自由度
キャラへの愛着を深める上で最高なのが、「名前・性別・ポートレートをいつでも自由に変更できる」という点です。
   作成時の一発勝負ではありません。「このキャラはやっぱり女性にしよう」「もっと強そうな顔グラ（ポートレート）に変えよう」といった変更が、ゲーム中いつでも可能です。自作画像の取り込みも容易で、システムに縛られることなく「自分だけの妄想パーティ」を完璧に再現できます。

 * 次回作にはない魅力！ 戦略的な「傭兵団運営」
実は、同シリーズの次回作（アーリーアクセス）は原点回帰し、シンプルなダンジョン探索のみに戻っています。だからこそ、今あえて本作『Godfall』を推したいのです。本作には、単なるダンジョン潜りにとどまらず、「傭兵団（ギルド）の運営」と「広大なワールドマップ」があります。拠点を拡張し、世界に影響力を広げていく感覚は、本作ならではの醍醐味。「冒険者たちを束ねる指揮官」として組織を大きくしていく、経営シム的な面白さは本作でしか味わえません。

 * ローグライト疲れに効く「積み上げ型」RPG
昨今は「死んだら終わり」のローグライクやローグライトが溢れていますが、本作は違います。パーマデス（キャラロスト）は強制されません。育てたキャラクター、集めた装備、拡張した拠点は確実に積み上がっていきます。「努力が無に帰すストレス」から解放され、じっくりと腰を据えて最強の部隊を作り上げることができます。

 * "おっさんゲーマー"に優しい、究極の快適設計
アクション要素が一切ない完全ターン制バトルは、コーヒー片手にじっくり思考を巡らせるのに最適です。シンボルエンカウント: 無駄な戦闘を避け、戦う相手を選べる戦略性。マッピング不要: オートマッピング完備。脱出ワンクリック: 「そろそろ帰ろうかな」と思ったら即帰還。ダンジョン探索の「面倒くさい部分」が徹底的に排除されており、美味しいところだけを味わえます。

 * 今こそ遊ぶべき理由：日本語化の充実
そして最大の朗報は、最近の有志による日本語化パッチの強化です。かつて言語の壁で敬遠していた方も、今ならストーリーやスキルの詳細を母国語で理解しながらプレイできます。敷居は劇的に下がりました。


総評：シリーズの中でも際立つ「隠れた名作」
最新の3Dグラフィックも、派手なアクションもありません。しかし、ここにはRPGというジャンルが本来持っていた「育成の喜び」と「戦術の快感」が凝縮されています。シンプルなダンジョン探索だけでは物足りない方、自分だけの最強ギルドを作り上げたい方へ。シリーズの中でも特に野心的な『Monsters' Den: Godfall』をお勧めします。

I was a fan of this franchise and played a lot of Monster Den Chronicles, back when you could only play the title in a browser with a low end PC. I was happy with this newer installment being super cheap during this winter sale so I had to try something that I loved in the past.

Sadly, the game had too many ideas that ended up not as harmonical as I would wish. A deal breaker for me was the fact that I have zero freedom regarding my initial party composition: You are stuck with a party early on consisting of: Mage, Cleric, Archer and Warrior... Veteran and old players would enjoy the chance of making wacky but useful/fun build like in previous Monsters' Den games: A full Conjurer + Mage party or a 2 Archer + 2 Warrior build... Being stuck in a basic party where you can't even add a Rogue or Warden early on really hurt the experience for me, and there is no reason on why such characters are locked so early when it wasn't a problem in any other franchise title.

But once the game gets going, I am surprised by the fact that missions now have a "timer": you can't walk freely and enjoy the map, if you don't head for your mission, you are done. Bounty system also expires/refresh every month so I wasted my first hour by not getting it done at all. The number of reputation points and currencies is a bit overwhelming for me.

Not only that, while the idea of a Keep with relics and also serving as a resting place and training for idle hired heroes is amazing, you pretty much have to pay RENT (maintenance of the Keep) in a video game and also a salary to your party of heroes (even though I did not choose my roster of mercenaries...). Monster Den series is hard enough so I would rather have some wagons with pavilions around for my ragtag band lacking good items or battle quickness early on (because as I said... No fast Rogue early with crits and no Warden with powerful Crossbows early on at all).

Different from the game before that one, I don't see so far how can I replay it with different strategies, since it feels a game that forces me to play in a way that I don't want to in the early game... Unless I get surprised later on in my journey, Monsters' Den: Godfall is a game that could have kept the original formula, added a few new features and granted the freedom from their rustic predecessors, but didn't... Maybe you should go for it in a Steam sale.

Monsters' Den: Godfall is a decent tactical turn-based dungeon crawler. It's simple and fast, but it doesn't do anything interesting and the basics aren't implemented that well.

I don't want to criticize this game too much, it does well what it tries to do. It's a straightforward dungeon crawl, the combat system is remeniscent of Wizardry games or rather ATB JRPGs. The story is an afterthought, the dungeons are simple and random, the combat is fast - this game is primarily about numbers go up. And there are too many inconsequential numbers for my tastes, growth doesn't have this interesting oompf to it. You go through an equipment threadmill, but very rarely there are interesting choices there.

Still you can do worse if you want a simple timekiller with some tactical depth. This game is very honest in what it is, and you may like it.

As someone who played Monster's Den on flash sites, this game scratches all the itch for the nostalgia and more. It's a huge expansion on everything, from mechanics to lore and worldbuilding. I like the new open-world approach, which is a surprisingly much needed break from the claustrophobic dungeon-crawling. Completing the main campaign makes you feel like you're actually saving the world (at least for now) instead of endlessly burrowing into a dungeon.

I also like the new classes that are 'remixes' of old classes which have 2 skill trees each. For example, I used to think clerics make no sense (healers that also do melee), and now we can have other classes that mix the healing skill tree with another more sensible skill tree. We can also have multiple party slots in a game so that I could tried out weird builds such as a full team with an assassin skill tree and stack poison damage (with relic) to kill bosses quickly.
Thank you for bringing this awesome classic to steam.

This game took everything I loved from the first two Monster's Den games namely...

1.) "Monster's Den The Book of Dread, which by the way was an OG Web Browser "Flash" game hosted on such awesome old-school web spaces like NewGrounds and Armor Games.

...and,

2.) Monster's Den Chronicles which was a worthy sequel also once hosted on freeware Flash game hosting sites.

... and tosses everything that made the core Monster's Den gameplay loop out the window in exchange for something absolutely irksome.

First they introduced an overly obtuse character development/Progression system that replaced the first two games' easier to understand character development mechanic.

Second, they removed health and mana potions in favor of a very stupid "Supply Pack" system that you can only use thrice to heal your characters, and what's worse is you can also use the pack to unlock locked chests costing you one valuable heal in favor of opening a chest with most likely trash loot.

3.) They made the in dungeon full recovery healing shrine COST Gold for you to use them. It wouldn't have been annoying IF the shrines were reusable seeing it costs gold to use, but nope... it's a one time, pay once use deal :P

Sure they added a "decent" plot story this time around, as well as an overworld map, and towns and such. But man did they  make this thing a huge slog to play. On that first dungeon mission the game gives you, I can't even beat the end dungeon boss even with the Warden NPC that joined my party and even if it was a five versus six fight, and my guys were at Level 3. The problem was, the boss kept healing himself and his mooks with my team not being able to do so ourselves.

Yeah Monster's Den is kind of a Difficult game at times, but this third game just made me Rage Quit hard :P

It's my type of game, with expendable characters that you can replace, an apparently non-linear story with a completely open world, and procedurally generated dungeons. All that is my thing. A game with those qualities would have to be extremely bad for me to not like it.

Combat is like what you'd see in an RPG maker game or JRPG or Darkest Dungeon, where you're not moving people around in tactical battles but selecting actions. It's alright. Not as good as DD, but alright. Dungeon exploration is fun.

Strangely enough considering you can retire characters and so on, this game does not have permadeath. Dead characters come back to life when you return to your base. I'd have preferred an Xcom approach, myself.

Thinking about it, I'd have a hard time recommending this game to people who were not specifically into this type of title. The tutorial doesn't make it clear how things work and you're constantly learning controls on the fly. There's a lot of:

"Oh, if I hover over this it tells me which rooms I haven't explored."
"Oh, dragging an item to that chest under these conditions puts it into the fortress vault."

Like there's room for all these different parties and characters, it looks like about 30 could fit into my guild along with 6 or 7 parties. But for some reason I'm capped at 4 total characters and I don't know why, and I don't know how I get more as none of the unlocks I can buy talks about that. Lots of stuff like that going on here.

But if you do like the type of features I talked about at the beginning, you know there aren't many games which have them and so Godfall is worth some money and time to you. Buying it at full price is a stretch but it goes on big sales (I got this at 66% off), and it's a good buy at that kind of price.

I waited on this game for a long while, but I'm glad I finally took the plunge. The mechanics, gameplay, and variety keeps me coming back, but it's not so deep I can't play it when I'm tired or don't have a lot of time for a session. I especially appreciate the loot variety, and how as you unlock more abilities and find more loot, your tactics will evolve and keep things fresh. So, I recommend this game if want an RGP that feels light but with enough crunch underneath it to give you some depth if you want it.

My one complaint is that I don't like the "advanced class" mechanic. You have to lock out your options to choose one, but you're already limited by hotbar space and the fact you may not use most of the abilities anyway (not to mention the base classes perform perfectly well on their own, a plus, honestly). I wish there were an option to let me try the advanced classes as true extras... then they'd feel like rewards earned instead of a dubious tradeoff to me.
